context:
Goal: a finished lane can be archived without a session guessing why the guard refused.
Problem (goal): The hook lane-closes-after-records refused archive_session twice with "the open pull requests of the lane's repo (shivinate7/mailaudit) could not be read". Cause, measured by the coordinator: its first add_repo used access read; the repo is public, so read attached nothing and the guard's gh could not read its open PRs; add_repo with access push fixed it. The refusal names no remedy, so a session cannot tell "cannot read" from "records not landed". You asked how to resolve this mechanically.
Based on (measured): the coordinator's own attach and retry, 11:4x to 13:10 CST Nov 17; step archive-refusal-names-add-repo already plans a remedy text, but it says "(read)", which fails for a public repo.
Departs from: main, where the hook refuses with no remedy and reads only through the session's gh; a changes how it reads, b changes only the text, c changes no code.
Waiting on: nothing stopped; the coordinator attaches with push meanwhile, and triage files your answer on the step.
Answered 13:11 CST Nov 17 in the coordinator's chat (relayed by the coordinator, 13:11 CST): option a, "approved". Closed 13:16 CST by triage 11. Filed on step archive-refusal-names-add-repo.

lastAnswer.note: a) Recommended. The guard reads a public repo's open PRs anonymously. The refusal names the route for a private repo: attach with add_repo access push, then retry. Then: approved.

options.gain: Fixes the cause for public repos and names the way out for private ones; no session has to guess.
options.how: A code change in the hook plus the refusal text.
options.label: The guard reads a public repo's open PRs anonymously over REST, and for a private repo the refusal says to attach it with add_repo access push, then retry
options.lose: A hook change that needs review rounds, and an anonymous read is rate limited.

options.gain: Cheapest; the existing step nearly covers it.
options.how: One sentence in the refusal; no new read.
options.label: Only the refusal text changes: it names the add_repo access push attach
options.lose: A public repo still needs the attach every time.

options.how: A standing rule for the coordinator.
options.label: The coordinator attaches every lane repo with push access at lane start; no guard change
options.lose: One attach per repo at every lane start, and the rule can be forgotten; the refusal still names no remedy.

title: A lane's archive was refused because the guard could not read its repo's open PRs, and the refusal named no way out. Which fix?
why: It fixes the cause for public repos and gives private repos a named remedy; b and c leave a public repo failing the same way.
